newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech spymaster quits in political spying row.
newsitem.headline: Czech spymaster quits in political spying row.

text.p: The acting director of the Czech state intelligence agency BIS resigned on Monday amid allegations it spied on a cabinet minister, the government said.

Government spokesman Ivo Strejcek told Reuters Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus had accepted Stanislav Devaty's resignation, which comes only days before Senate elections, the first test of the centre-right coalition since it lost its lower house majority six months ago.
Last Friday Agriculture Minister Josef Lux accused the BIS of spying on him three years ago.
Klaus said on Sunday that the probe had been aimed not at Lux, who heads the Christian Democrats, junior partners in the ruling coalition, but at one of his advisers, Antonin Moravec.
Moravec was the head of a bank which collapsed amidst a fraud scandal in 1993 and had business links with a former communist general.

Devaty, who has never been confirmed as BIS director even though he has been in the job for several years, is a member of Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) although he suspended his membership when he became the country's spymaster.
Last year another junior member of Klaus's coalition, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODS), also alleged it had been the victim of BIS spying. Those allegations were never substantiated.
